LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.4: Oral Expression
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Expression, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to keep a routine? 2. How do non- verbal cues support oral communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline activities carried out daily at home in their order of sequence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline activities carried out daily at home in their order of sequence,

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home,

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe their daily routine and make entries in a diary,

2. organise the activities carried out in a day in order of sequence,

3. work jointly to make a presentation of daily home routines while using appropriate non-verbal cues,

4. peer assess each other’s use of non-verbal cues for constructive feedback. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe their daily routine and make entries in a diary,
2. organise the activities carried out in a day in order of sequence,
3. work jointly to make a presentation of daily home routines while using appropriate non-verbal cues,
4. peer assess each other’s use of non-verbal cues for constructive feedback. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Expression together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner builds on their own learning experiences by observing their daily routine

and makes entries in a diary.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows defining personal skills when peer-assessing each other’s use of non- verbal cues for constructive feedback.

8

Values:
Respect: This is enhanced as the learner shows positive regard for self and others while working to make a presentation of daily

home routines while using appropriate non-verbal cues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner interacts with information building on time management skills when talking about

telling time.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the concept on time to their learning of similar content in Mathematics.
